title: The sacrament’s meaning matters more than what is on the table
setting: In August 1830, Newel and Sally Knight visited Joseph and Emma Smith at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Emma and Sally had not yet been confirmed, and the group planned to confirm them and take the sacrament. Joseph reported that a heavenly messenger met him as he went to buy wine. He wrote the first paragraph then; his later history says the rest was written in September. The longer text was first printed in the 1835 Doctrine and Covenants.
summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ. It says that what the Saints eat or drink in the sacrament does not matter if they remember his body and blood. It forbids buying wine or strong drink from enemies and allows only wine made new among themselves. It promises that Christ will drink of the fruit of the vine with his servants on the earth. It names those who will join him: Moroni, Elias, John the Baptist, Elijah, the patriarchs, Michael or Adam, and Peter, James, and John. It says John ordained Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery to the first priesthood. It says Peter, James, and John ordained them apostles and gave them keys. It ends by telling them to put on “my whole armor” and stand.

contextNote.title: Remembrance, not the cup, is the point
contextNote.text: Joseph reported that this revelation came as he went to buy wine. Verse 2 says “it mattereth not” what is eaten or drunk in the sacrament. What matters is doing it “with an eye single to my glory”. The verse then names what is to be remembered: a body laid down and blood shed for sins. Verses 3–4 add a practical rule against buying wine from enemies. In this passage the sacrament is defined by remembrance, and the emblems serve that remembrance.

ldsText: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “All Things Must Be Done in Order” uses this revelation to focus the sacrament on remembering Christ. The Church now uses water, as verse 2 allows; what in verse 2 will you deliberately remember at the sacrament this week?
reviewNote: Read all 18 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, August 1830, a messenger met Joseph as he went for wine, part recorded then and the rest the next September. JSP historical introduction read for the Knights’ visit and the dating: 1833 printings gave 4 September 1830; the expanded text first appears in the 1835 D&C. Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Zacharias, and Aaron are named in the text but are not in people-ids; not added. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote opening stated the revelation’s interruption as fact; now attributed to Joseph’s report.
